questions.stem: What happens to blood vessels near the skin when the body is too hot?

options.text: They constrict to trap heat inside the body
They dilate to allow more blood to flow near the skin, increasing heat loss
They close completely to prevent blood reaching the skin
They remain unchanged while only sweating increases

questions.explanation: When the body is too hot, vasodilation occurs. Blood vessels near the skin surface widen, allowing more blood to flow close to the surface so heat can be lost to the environment by radiation.
